title: Permanence and separation for ind-quasi-affine morphisms
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Say $f$ has property $P$ if, for every affine open $U\subset Y$ and every quasi-compact open $K\subset f^{-1}(U)$, the induced morphism $K\to U$ is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]. Then (1) $P$ is preserved by arbitrary base change [def-pc-fibre-product]; (2) if $Y=\bigcup_i U_i$ is any affine open cover, $P(f)$ holds if and only if $P(f^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i)$ holds for every $i$; (3) if $Y$ is affine and $P(f)$ holds, every quasi-compact open of $X$ is a quasi-affine scheme (a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme), and $X$ is separated, hence quasi-separated [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

proof.text: Define Q(X) to mean that every quasi-compact open of X is a quasi-affine scheme. Q is inherited by an open subscheme: send a quasi-compact open to its open image, use compactness of continuous images, and transport quasi-affineness along the open-image isomorphism. Over an affine target A, a map K → A with quasi-compact source K is quasi-compact because A is quasi-separated. Thus the source-library instances give IsQuasiAffineHom(K → A) iff K.IsQuasiAffine. Use the canonical isomorphism between the pullback over an open inclusion and the inverse-image open subscheme to identify P(f) with targetAffineLocally Q(f).

Make Q an affine-target local morphism property. Isomorphism invariance and restriction to basic opens follow from inheritance by open subschemes. To descend from a basic-open cover of an affine target, apply lem-a1-qc-open-quasi-affine-chart-descent with V equal to the whole target; its last clause says that every quasi-compact open of the whole source is quasi-affine. Mathlib HasAffineProperty.of_iSup_eq_top now gives the reverse implication of clause (2) for an arbitrary affine open cover, using the pullback/restriction isomorphism. The forward implication follows from base-change stability proved next.

For maps a:X → A and b:B → A with A and B affine and Q(X), apply lem-a1-qc-open-pullback-quasi-affine-enlargement to each quasi-compact open L of X ×_A B. Its L-quasi-affine conclusion proves Q(X ×_A B). Transport across pullback symmetry for the projection convention used by Mathlib AffineTargetMorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange.mk. Mathlib HasAffineProperty.isStableUnderBaseChange extends this affine-target calculation to arbitrary bases and arbitrary base changes. Applying pullback_snd proves clause (1) and the forward direction of clause (2).

If Y is affine, HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine identifies P(f) with Q(X), which gives the first conclusion in clause (3). For affine opens A,B of X, their union is quasi-compact by compactness of affine opens and finite-union compactness, so Q(X) makes it quasi-affine and hence separated by lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding. Use W=A∪B in lem-a1-separated-affine-pair-neighbourhoods. Its separatedness and quasi-separatedness conclusions, together with Mathlib quasiSeparatedSpace_iff_quasiSeparated, give the rest of clause (3).

lean.statement: theorem indQuasiAffineProperty_permanence {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ Y), indQuasiAffineProperty f → indQuasiAffineProperty (Limits.pullback.snd f g)) ∧ (∀ {I : Type v} (U : I → Y.Opens), (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) → iSup U = ⊤ → (indQuasiAffineProperty f ↔ ∀ i, indQuasiAffineProperty (Limits.pullback.snd f (U i).ι))) ∧ (∀ (_hY : IsAffine Y), indQuasiAffineProperty f → (∀ (K : X.Opens), IsCompact (K : Set X) → K.toScheme.IsQuasiAffine) ∧ Scheme.IsSeparated X ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
lean.note: The helper predicate indQuasiAffineProperty is the exact P condition stated in the node; the theorem gives all three clauses. The pullback presentation is the canonical scheme model of the inverse image over an affine open.
